newsitem.title: PERU: Japan's Ikeda arrives to congratulate Fujimori.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Ikeda arrives to congratulate Fujimori.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda arrived in Lima early on Thursday to congratulate President Alberto Fujimori and hear firsthand how Peru's military ended the 18-week-long hostage crisis.

Ikeda, who travelled with family members of the two dozen Japanese diplomats and businessmen among 71 hostages rescued in Tuesday's daring assault, was met by Peruvian Prime Minister Alberto Pandolfi at Lima's military airport on his arrival soon after midnight local time (0500 GMT).
"His visit is to express thanks for the results of this operation to free the hostages from the house of the Japanese ambassador," Pandolfi told reporters.
Ikeda was due to meet Fujimori on Thursday afternoon.

During a visit of three or four days, Ikeda also planned to visit some of the two dozen Japanese diplomats and businessmen among the hostages, and offer his condolences to the families of the captive and two soldiers who died in the rescue operation.
He was also due to supervise the re-opening of the Japanese Embassy in Lima.
Ikeda's delegation of Foreign Ministry and military officials, businessmen, relatives and journalists totalled about 120 people, local radio reported.
Ikeda had previously visited Peru in the days after the takeover of the residence by a band of jungle-trained rebels as Tokyo tried to restrain Fujimori from an immediate violent option.
All 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels were killed in Tuesday's assault, which was ordered without Japan's knowledge by Peru's President Alberto Fujimori.
